added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We give the deterministic charging and the probability calculation.  They are conditional on \(\mathcal F_1\), so \(\eta\) is fixed and independent of the second-half observations by independent sampling.  Write \(P_X=P\circ X^{-1}\).  For \(x=(0,s)\), \(h=\eta(x)\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), write
\[
 A(x,t)=A_t\cap B_2(x,h),\qquad p(x,t)=P\{X\in A(x,t)\}.
\]
The base-mass condition gives \(p(x,t)\geq a_P(x,h)>0\).  Conditional on all scores, independence and the conditional sub-Gaussian assumption imply
\[
 E_P\!\left[\exp\!\left\{\lambda
 \sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\right\}
 \middle|X_1,\ldots,X_n,\mathcal F_1\right]
 \leq \exp\!\left\{\frac{\lambda^2\sigma^2N_2(A)}2\right\}       \tag{M3}
\]
for every selected set \(A\), where \(N_2(A)=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\).  Exponential Markov applied to \(\lambda\) and \(-\lambda\), followed by minimization in \(\lambda\), gives
\[
 P\!\left\{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\right|
 >\sigma\sqrt{2N_2(A)z}\,\middle|X_1,\ldots,X_n,\mathcal F_1\right\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                        \tag{M4}
\]

We next prove the multiscale count used to spend the tail probabilities in \((\mathrm{M4})\).  Associate with \(A(x,t)\) the untruncated boundary interval
\[
 I(x)=[s-h,s+h].
\]
For centers on the vertical line, \(I(x)\subseteq I(x')\) is equivalent to
\(|s-s'|+h\leq h'\), and this implies
\(B_2(x,h)\subseteq B_2(x',h')\).  At one fixed \(h\) and in one dyadic mass cell with ceiling \(u\), choose greedily, from left to right, a maximal \(h/2\)-separated list of centers and call them the fixed-scale roots.  Every remaining center is within \(h/2\) of a root.  For a fixed score \((r_i,s_i)\) with \(|r_i|\leq h\), membership as the center coordinate varies is the indicator of
\([s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}]\); otherwise it is identically zero.  Thus a left-to-right sweep through a cluster charges the score with at most one entrance and one exit.  The ordered root list splits into its odd and even sublists, each of which is \(h\)-separated.  Hence, for every \(u\geq0\), the number of fixed-scale roots whose centers satisfy \(a_P(x,h)\leq u\) is at most
\[
 2\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}.                                                \tag{M5}
\]

For completeness, here is the varying-radius construction.  First order the selected intervals by decreasing dyadic radius, then by left endpoint, then by right endpoint, retaining one representative for each selected second-half membership pattern.  Attach an interval to the least earlier interval containing it; if none exists, declare it a root.  For the half-disks on one fixed treatment side, two noncoincident circular boundary arcs whose centers lie on \(B\) intersect at most once: subtracting their two squared-circle equations leaves an affine equation in the boundary coordinate.  Consequently the exposed left arcs and exposed right arcs of the noncontained children are each endpoint-monotone.  Sweep these two lists separately.  Membership of any fixed score in a swept list is consecutive, because a second entrance after an exit would force two intersections of the corresponding exposed arcs.  On each list, cut whenever the \(P_X\)-mass newly entered or left since the preceding cut first exceeds \(2^{-r}u\), where \(u\) is the parent's mass ceiling.  Every set in the list is contained in the parent and every score enters and leaves at most once, so each list has total entered-plus-left mass at most \(2u\).  Thus at charge depth \(r\) there are at most
\[
 2^{r+2}\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}                                         \tag{M6}
\]
charged blocks issued from the roots in \((\mathrm{M5})\), and every block has \(P_X\)-mass at most \(2^{-r}u\).  For roots of different radii in the same mass and variance cell, let \(h_*\) be the smallest radius.  Monotonicity of ball mass gives
\(a_P(x,h_*)\leq a_P(x,h_x)\leq u\) for every root center.  Greedy clustering at distance \(h_*/2\), followed by odd/even splitting, leaves at most
\(2\{1\vee J_P(h_*,u)\}\) clusters; the two exposed-arc sweeps control all roots inside a cluster.  The root having radius \(h_*\) belongs to the selected family, so the supremum in \((\mathrm{M7})\) contains the logarithmic charge for this common packing count.  Intervals of equal endpoint or equal radius are assigned by the displayed deterministic tie order, so every selected pattern is charged exactly once.  An infinite center family causes no difficulty: on fixed second-half scores it has finitely many membership patterns, and monotone convergence passes from these finite representatives to the supremum.

Let
\[
 \Lambda(x)=1+\log\!\left(
 e\left\{1\vee J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h)\}\right)\right\}\right),
 \qquad
 R=\sup_{x\in B}\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(x)}{n_2a_P(x,h)}}.       \tag{M7}
\]
For each cell, either its expected count is at least \(64\Lambda(x)\), or its normalized oracle scale is already bounded below by a numerical multiple of \(\sigma\):
\[
 n_2a_P(x,h)\geq64\Lambda(x)
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(x)}{n_2a_P(x,h)}}>\frac\sigma8.       \tag{M8}
\]
Peel the roots simultaneously by the dyadic values of \(h\), of \(a_P(x,h)\), and of \(p(x,t)/a_P(x,h)\).  In a cell with mass ceiling \(u\), equations \((\mathrm{M5})\)--\((\mathrm{M6})\) and the definition of \(\Lambda\) show that the number of depth-\(r\) blocks is at most
\(2^{r+2}e^{\Lambda-1}\).  A depth-\(r\) block has variance proxy at most \(2^{-r}n_2u\sigma^2\).  Applying \((\mathrm{M4})\) to its increment at threshold
\[
 C\sigma\sqrt{n_2u\{\Lambda+z\}}
\]
therefore spends at most
\[
 2^{r+3}e^{\Lambda-1}
 \exp\{-c2^r(\Lambda+z)\}.                                         \tag{M9}
\]
Summing \((\mathrm{M9})\) over \(r\geq0\) is at most \(C e^{-cz}\).  Passing from one side-mass cell to the next multiplies the numerator standard deviation by \(2^{1/2}\) and the reciprocal count by \(2^{-1}\); hence its contribution to an average is multiplied by \(2^{-1/2}\).  Summing \(\sum_{j\geq0}2^{-j/2}<\infty\) pays all side-mass severity cells.  The dyadic radius forest is already included in \((\mathrm{M6})\): contained intervals are increments paid by \((\mathrm{M9})\), while incomparable radii in a common mass-variance cell are clustered at their smallest radius and paid by its packing count.  Moving to a smaller variance cell gives the same \(2^{-1/2}\) factor.  Consequently neither the number of radii nor the number of mass cells appears in the threshold.

Apply the same forest calculation to the centered Bernoulli variables
\(\mathbf 1\{X_i\in A\}-P_X(A)\).  On the first alternative in \((\mathrm{M8})\), the Bernoulli exponential-moment bound implies that the forest probability of
\(N_2(A)<n_2P_X(A)/2\) is summable, because a cell having packing charge \(e^{\Lambda-1}\) has lower-tail probability at most \(e^{-8\Lambda}\).  On the complementary event, every selected set has
\[
 N_2(A)\geq \tfrac12n_2P_X(A),                                     \tag{M10}
\]
On \((\mathrm{M10})\), divide the increment bounds from \((\mathrm{M9})\) by \(N_2(A)\), telescope along each root-to-leaf path, and use \((\mathrm{M7})\).  On the lower-count complement, peel the positive counts into
\(2^{-d-1}n_2P_X(A)<N_2(A)\leq2^{-d}n_2P_X(A)\).  The Bernoulli lower-tail exponent is still at least \(c n_2P_X(A)\), whereas \((\mathrm{M4})\)'s average threshold grows only as \(2^{d/2}\); summing in \(d\) gives the same constant multiple of \(R\).  Cells in the second alternative of \((\mathrm{M8})\) are handled by the same positive-count peeling starting at \(d=0\); their oracle scale is at least \(\sigma/8\), and the factor \(e^{\Lambda-1}\) is paid by the \(\Lambda\) term in \((\mathrm{M9})\).  Thus, for every \(z\geq1\),
\[
 P\!\left\{
 \sup_{x,t:N_t^{(2)}(x,h)>0}
 \frac{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A(x,t)\}\right|}{N_t^{(2)}(x,h)}
 >CR(1+\sqrt z)\,\middle|\mathcal F_1\right\}
 \leq Ce^{-cz}.                                                      \tag{M11}
\]
Finally, integrate \((\mathrm{M11})\), using
\(E Z=\int_0^\infty P(Z>v)\,dv\) for a nonnegative random variable and
\(\int_1^\infty e^{-cz}\,dz<\infty\).  This proves \((\mathrm{M2})\), since its displayed additive remainder is nonnegative.  Every division used \((\mathrm{M10})\), a peeled positive count, or the explicit positive-count restriction, and every logarithm is defined because of \(1\vee J_P\).
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma replaces an informal varying-bandwidth charging step by an explicit interval forest, fixed-radius odd/even roots, mass-drop increments, and a summable conditional tail budget.
added_lemmas.gap: A fixed-bandwidth entropy bound does not by itself control the sample-selected bandwidth map without paying for all radii; the interval forest proves that contained scales are paid as variance-decaying increments.
added_lemmas.consumer: The profile oracle theorem uses the lemma to obtain its selected-bandwidth stochastic bound without a global logarithmic penalty.

added_lemmas.statement:
There are constants \(c,C\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) with
\(\inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)
\geq1-Cn^{-3}\) such that, simultaneously for \(h\in H_n\) and
\(u\in U_n\) satisfying \(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\),
\[
 J_P(h,u)\leq
 \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)
 \leq
 C\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)\right\}.                 \tag{P1}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\) for every
\(x,h\), and the bounds are within constant factors when
\(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\).  For every \(h\in H_n\), the source-labeled
lexicographic sorting, duplicate removal, and midpoint map defining
\(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\);
the finite maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,u)\) is therefore Borel for every
\(u\in U_n\).  The confidence calibration, zero-count event, and
\(h_0\)-fallback event together contribute at most
\(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\) to expected supremum risk and introduce no
leading global \(\log n\) factor on \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell=\log(en)\).  If \(m=0\), the condition
\(mu\geq C\ell\) has no solutions, so the assertion containing \(\ell/m\) is never evaluated; the definitions with \(m\vee1\) still give
\(q_t^L=0\leq q_t\leq1=q_t^U\).  We may therefore take \(m\geq1\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(s\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(h\in H_n\), define
\[
 C_{t,s,h}=\{z\in A_t:\|z-(0,s)\|_2\leq h\}.
\]
On deterministic points \(z_i=(r_i,s_i)\), membership of \(z_i\) in
\(C_{t,s,h}\), as a function of \(s\), is the indicator of the closed interval
\[
 \left[s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}\right]             \tag{P2}
\]
when \(z_i\in A_t\) and \(|r_i|\leq h\), and is identically zero otherwise.
Thus, for fixed \(t,h\), the trace on \(N\) points changes only at the at most
\(2N\) endpoints in \((\mathrm{P2})\).  Since
\(|H_n|\leq2+\log_2 n\), the shatter coefficient of
\[
 \mathcal C_n=\{C_{t,s,h}:t\in\{0,1\},\ s\in[-1/2,1/2],\ h\in H_n\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(N)\leq2|H_n|(2N+1)\leq C_0(N+1)\ell.           \tag{P3}
\]

We spell out the relative-deviation step.  If \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are Bernoulli with mean \(p\), exponential Markov and
\(e^v-1-v\leq v^2/[2(1-|v|/3)]\) for \(|v|<3\) give
\[
 P\!\left\{|\widehat p-p|>
 2\sqrt{3p z/m}+6z/m\right\}\leq2e^{-z}.                           \tag{P4}
\]
Introduce an independent ghost sample of size \(m\).  On the event in which
\(|P_m(C)-P(C)|\) exceeds twice the right-hand deviation scale, conditional Chebyshev applied to the ghost count gives probability at least \(1/2\) that
\(|P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|\) exceeds one half of that scale.  Conditional on the pooled \(2m\) observations, random signs exchange the two halves.  Applying \((\mathrm{P4})\) to those signs and taking a union over the at most
\(\Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(2m)\) pooled traces yields
\[
 P\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal C_n:\ |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{12P_m(C)\ell/m}+20\ell/m\right\}
 \leq8\Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(2m)e^{-6\ell}.                            \tag{P5}
\]
To pass from the population variance in \((\mathrm{P4})\) to the empirical variance in \((\mathrm{P5})\), write
\(d=|P_m(C)-P(C)|\), use
\(\sqrt{P(C)}\leq\sqrt{P_m(C)}+\sqrt d\), and apply
\(2ab\leq a^2+b^2\) to absorb \(d/2\) into the left side.  This gives the displayed constants.  By \((\mathrm{P3})\), the right side of \((\mathrm{P5})\) is at most \(C_1n^{-3}\).  Closed intervals in \((\mathrm{P2})\) ensure that the union includes breakpoint traces rather than merely open cells.

Let \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) be the event complementary to that in \((\mathrm{P5})\).  Since
\(P_m(C_{t,s,h})=\widehat q_t^{(1)}((0,s),h)\), the definitions of
\(b_n,q_t^L,q_t^U\) give on \(\mathcal E_{1n}\), simultaneously in \(x,t,h\),
\[
 q_t^L(x,h)\leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h).                           \tag{P6}
\]
Taking minima over \(t\) gives
\[
 a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h).                              \tag{P7}
\]
Solving the quadratic inequality in \((\mathrm{P5})\) shows that, whenever
\(mq_t(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\),
\[
 \tfrac12q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^L(x,h)
 \leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)\leq2q_t(x,h).                        \tag{P8}
\]
If \(ma_P(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), both side masses satisfy the premise of
\((\mathrm{P8})\); hence
\[
 \tfrac12a_P(x,h)\leq a^L(x,h)
 \leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\leq2a_P(x,h).                         \tag{P9}
\]
Moreover, \(a^L(x,h)>0\) implies
\(\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h)>b_n(\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h))\) on both sides.  Squaring this inequality and using the linear term in \(b_n\) gives
\(m\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h)\geq c\ell\); equation \((\mathrm{P5})\) then gives \(mq_t(x,h)\geq c'\ell\).  Thus, after one fixed enlargement of the constant in \((\mathrm{P8})\), the factor comparison \((\mathrm{P9})\) applies to every empirically admissible pair.

Fix \(h\).  Every sample breakpoint in \((\mathrm{P2})\) is entered in the candidate list with its coordinate, sample index, and sign.  Lexicographic order is total.  If labels tie in coordinate, retaining the least label deletes only duplicate labels and retains the coordinate.  A deterministic mesh point tied with a breakpoint likewise occurs once in the sorted set.  Define \(g_h((0,s))\) as follows: at a breakpoint, a mesh point, or an endpoint of \(B\), take \(g_h((0,s))=(0,s)\); in the unique open interval \((w_j,w_{j+1})\) containing any other \(s\), take
\(g_h((0,s))=(0,(w_j+w_{j+1})/2)\).  There is no sample breakpoint in that open interval, so all empirical membership indicators are constant there.  Moreover
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2\leq\frac1{2M_h}\leq\frac h{32}<\frac h4,
 \qquad
 \widehat q_t^{(1)}(g_h(x),h)=\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h)               \tag{P10}
\]
for both sides.  At a breakpoint equality in \((\mathrm{P10})\) follows because the ball is closed; thus all endpoint and coincident-breakpoint ties are covered.

Let \(F\) be an \(h\)-separated subset of
\(\{x:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\).  For each \(x\in F\), choose
\(t_x\) with \(q_{t_x}(x,h)\leq u\).  Equations \((\mathrm{P5})\) and
\((\mathrm{P10})\) give
\[
 a^U(g_h(x),h)\leq C_3\{u+\ell/m\}.                               \tag{P11}
\]
For distinct \(x,x'\in F\),
\[
 \|g_h(x)-g_h(x')\|_2
 \geq h-h/32-h/32=15h/16>h/2.                                     \tag{P12}
\]
The upward severity rounding obeys
\(u(v)\leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\}\).  Taking \(c\geq2C_3+1\), equations
\((\mathrm{P11})\)--\((\mathrm{P12})\) show that \(g_h(F)\) is feasible in the finite maximum defining
\(\widehat J(h,c\{u+\ell/m\})\).  The map is injective by \((\mathrm{P12})\), so
\[
 J_P(h,u)\leq\widehat J(h,c\{u+\ell/m\}).                          \tag{P13}
\]

Conversely, if \(G\) is a nonempty feasible set in the finite maximum defining
\(\widehat J(h,v)\), then \((\mathrm{P7})\) and severity rounding give, for every \(g\in G\),
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\leq u(v)
 \leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\}.                                         \tag{P14}
\]
Order \(G=\{g_1<\cdots<g_M\}\) along \(B\).  Feasibility gives
\(\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h/2\), and therefore
\[
 \|g_{j+2}-g_j\|_2
 =\|g_{j+2}-g_{j+1}\|_2+\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h.                 \tag{P15}
\]
Thus the odd and even sublists are each \(h\)-separated.  Crucially,
\((\mathrm{P14})\) already makes every point thin at radius \(h\); no monotonicity argument and no radius shrink are needed.  Each sublist has cardinality at most
\(J_P(h,2v+m^{-1})\), whence
\[
 |G|\leq2J_P(h,2v+m^{-1}).                                        \tag{P16}
\]
If the feasible maximum is zero, the outer floor in \(\widehat J\) equals one.  Combining this case with \((\mathrm{P16})\), substituting
\(v=c\{u+\ell/m\}\), and enlarging \(C\) proves the same-radius upper inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\), with the necessary \(1\vee J_P\) protection.

All maps just used are Borel.  The square-root breakpoint is continuous on its closed domain; candidate inclusion and lexicographic comparisons are Borel; sorting and duplicate removal require finitely many such comparisons.  Deterministic refinement and midpoint formation are Borel.  Finally, \(G_1(h)\) is finite, so \(\widehat J(h,u)\) is the maximum of finitely many Borel feasibility indicators.

It remains to verify the risk remainder stated in the lemma.  Choose
\(h^\circ\in H_n\) satisfying
\[
 n^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}\leq h^\circ<2n^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}.           \tag{P17}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), such a grid point exists.  The base-mass condition, \(n_2\asymp n\), \(h^\circ\leq1\), and
\(\kappa\leq\bar\kappa\) imply
\[
 \inf_{x\in B}n_2a_P(x,h^\circ)
 \geq c n(h^\circ)^{\bar\kappa}\geq c n^{3/4}.                   \tag{P18}
\]
The deterministic packing bound on the unit-length segment is
\(1\vee J_P(h,u)\leq1+h^{-1}\).  Equations \((\mathrm{P1})\),
\((\mathrm{P9})\), and \((\mathrm{P18})\) therefore make \(h^\circ\) admissible at every \(x\), outside a probability \(Cn^{-3}\), and bound its criterion by
\[
 d_n=C\{Ln^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}+\sigma n^{-3/8}\sqrt\ell\}.         \tag{P19}
\]
Minimization gives the same bound at \(\widehat h(x)\).  Since the stochastic term in the criterion is present and its logarithmic numerator is at least one,
\[
 \inf_{x\in B}n_2a_P(x,\widehat h(x))
 \geq c d_n^{-2}\geq c n^{1/(2\bar\kappa)}.                       \tag{P20}
\]
Applying the relative-deviation calculation \((\mathrm{P3})\)--\((\mathrm{P5})\) to the independent second half and using \((\mathrm{P20})\) shows that a selected side count is zero with probability at most \(Cn^{-3}\), uniformly in \(P\).  The empty-admissible-set event is already excluded by \((\mathrm{P18})\).  Projection bounds the loss by \(4L\) on these events and on \(\mathcal E_{1n}^c\).  Tail integration in the multiscale selected-interval lemma bounds the remaining confidence-calibration tail by
\(C\sigma\ell^2/n\).  Hence the combined expected contribution is at most
\[
 C(L+\sigma)\ell^2/n.                                               \tag{P21}
\]

Finally fix \(P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\), let
\(b=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and choose \(h_b\in H_n\) with
\(b\leq h_b<2b\).  Write
\(a_P(x,h_b)=w_x h_b^\kappa\); base mass gives \(w_x\geq c_m\).  The isolated envelope, including its \(u=1\) endpoint when the severity is clipped, gives
\[
 J_P\!\left(h_b,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h_b)\}\right)
 \leq C\{1+w_x^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}.                                  \tag{P22}
\]
Compactness of the exponent window implies
\[
 \sup_{\substack{\kappa\in K\\w\geq c_m}}
 \frac{1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee C(1+w^{1/(\kappa-2)})\}\right)}w<\infty. \tag{P23}
\]
Because \(nh_b^\kappa\asymp h_b^{-2}\), equations \((\mathrm{P9})\), \((\mathrm{P16})\), and \((\mathrm{P22})\)--\((\mathrm{P23})\) show that \(h_b\) is empirically admissible and that its empirical criterion is at most \(Cb\), uniformly in \(x\).  Minimization therefore gives the same bound at \(\widehat h(x)\).  Conversely, the representative construction \((\mathrm{P10})\)--\((\mathrm{P13})\), applied at the local severity of an admissible selected pair, gives for the constant \(C_0\) in the multiscale lemma
\[
 1\vee J_P\!\left(\widehat h(x),
 \min\{1,C_0a_P(x,\widehat h(x))\}\right)
 \leq \widehat J\!\left(\widehat h(x),
 \widehat u(x,\widehat h(x))\right).                              \tag{P24}
\]
Here \(C_0\) is chosen below the fixed factor four in the definition of \(\widehat u\); equation \((\mathrm{P9})\) supplies the required relative-mass comparison.  The admissibility inequality, \((\mathrm{P9})\), \((\mathrm{P24})\), and the selected criterion bound now imply
\[
 \sup_{x\in B}\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee J_P(\widehat h(x),
 \min\{1,C_0a_P(x,\widehat h(x))\})\}\right)}
 {n_2a_P(x,\widehat h(x))}}
 \leq Cb.                                                         \tag{P25}
\]
The multiscale lemma and the Lipschitz bias bound consequently give an \(O(b)\) contribution.  The remainder in \((\mathrm{P21})\) is \(o(b)\), uniformly on \(K\).  Thus neither the severity peeling nor the dyadic bandwidth selection contributes a leading global logarithm.  The unit floor contributes only \(\log e=1\).  This proves every assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: The same-radius upper comparison follows directly because every empirical qualifier is already population-thin at radius \(h\); odd/even splitting upgrades only the separation from \(h/2\) to \(h\).
added_lemmas.gap: The prior radius-shrunk statement obscured the oracle actually available from the construction and left the varying-bandwidth stochastic charge informal.
added_lemmas.consumer: Inbound dependencies of the former packing lemma migrate to this sharper result, so the population oracle uses the profile at the estimator's own radius and retains \(1\vee J_P\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix any \(\kappa_0\in K\) and \(c_2>0\).  There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on the fixed model constants and uniformly over laws
\(P\in\mathrm{Base}_{\kappa_0}\) which additionally satisfy
\[
 a_P(x,h)\geq c_2h^2
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in B\text{ and }0<h\leq h_0,             \tag{R1}
\]
the same total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\), without knowledge of
\(\kappa_0\), \(c_2\), or a profile label, obeys for all sufficiently large \(n\)
\[
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/4}.                       \tag{R2}
\]
This is a regular-design corollary for the sub-Gaussian overlap of the present model with a positive-density boundary design; it is not a transfer of results stated for the full positive-density class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\), and choose \(h_r\in H_n\) with
\(r_n\leq h_r<2r_n\), which is possible for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Every \(h\)-separated subset of the unit-length segment \(B\) has at most
\(1+h^{-1}\leq2h^{-1}\) points because \(h\leq h_0\leq1/8\).  Therefore
\[
 1\vee J_P(h,u)\leq2h^{-1}                                        \tag{R3}
\]
for every \(u\geq0\).  The population oracle inequality for
\(\widehat\tau_n\), condition \((\mathrm{R1})\), and \((\mathrm{R3})\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 &\leq C\left\{Lh_r+\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{1+\log(2e/h_r)}{nc_2h_r^2}}\right\}
 +C(L+\sigma)\frac{\log^2(en)}n\\
 &\leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/4}.                     \tag{R4}
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, \(h_r^2=(\log n/n)^{1/2}\), so the square-root term in the first line of \((\mathrm{R4})\) is \(O(r_n)\), and
\(\log^2(en)/n=o(r_n)\).  Every denominator is positive by \((\mathrm{R1})\).  The estimator's construction contains none of \(\kappa_0,c_2\), or the class label.  The established isolated and pervasive endpoint corollary applies to this same map, which yields one procedure across the three regimes.

The empirical packing count now has a proved same-radius upper comparison: equation \(a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\) and odd/even splitting yield \(\widehat J(h,v)\leq C\{1\vee J_P(h,C(v+\log(en)/n_1))\}\). The resulting oracle gives the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and, under quadratic side mass, the regular rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for the same procedure.

sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. For each \(x\in B\), the lower side-mass bound puts \(x\) in the support of both restricted score laws. Sharp assignment and consistency make the observed side regression equal to \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere on side \(t\); the declared Lipschitz representative is continuous and unique on that support. Therefore its observed-side limit at \(x\) equals \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and subtracting the two limits identifies \(\tau_P(x)=\theta_{1,P}(x)-\theta_{0,P}(x)\).

prose_updates.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies pointwise rates for univariate regularly varying designs. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise smoothness adaptation; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas the present \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate inhomogeneous designs with finitely many zeros and spatially normalized uniform loss. Those classes are neither asserted to contain nor to be contained in the present two-sided boundary profile classes, so no theorem is transferred directly. Antoniadis, Pensky, and Sapatinas (2014) likewise study global adaptation in a univariate inhomogeneous design, and Bertin (2004) supplies a positive-density supremum benchmark. Chen and Gao (2026) concern scalar submanifold integrals under positive bounded design density, not an entire depleted boundary trace. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu impose continuous density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. The regular-design corollary is identified only with the sub-Gaussian overlap of their positive-density class; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Likewise, a converse restricted to a specified estimator or decision class remains estimator-restricted and is not used as an unrestricted minimax converse here. The new component is the same-radius protected packing oracle and its multiscale selected-bandwidth proof.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Scalar side mass does not imply coercivity of higher-order local-polynomial Gram matrices, so the estimator uses local averages. It treats \(L\) and \(\sigma\) as fixed known class constants. Constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from \(2\). The regular-design comparison covers only laws satisfying the present conditional sub-Gaussian condition as well as quadratic one-sided mass; it is not a claim about the full positive-density comparator class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The closed novelty claim is the same-radius profile-packing oracle inequality, including the multiscale selected-interval bound that removes the informal varying-bandwidth charge. The unit floor \(1\vee J_P\) is retained everywhere because \(\widehat J\geq1\) even for an empty population thin set; it contributes only a numerical constant. The same total estimator attains the regular \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), isolated \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and pervasive \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) upper rates under their stated law conditions. Identification is a supporting observed-law argument, not the headline. The endpoint minimax orders remain attributed to the banked parent result. No arbitrary-profile exactness, local-oracle band claim, transfer from a full Cattaneo--Titiunik--Yu class, or unrestricted use of an estimator-restricted converse is asserted.
